**Tallest building in each of the five Indian cities (as of 2024)**  

| City | Building (as listed on Wikipedia) | Height (m / ft) | Floors* | Year the structure topped‑out / was completed (or expected) | Primary use | Wikipedia source |
|------|-----------------------------------|----------------|--------|-----------------------------------------------------------|------------|-------------------|
| **Mumbai** | **Palais Royale** (residential‑hotel tower) | **320 m / 1,050 ft** | **88** | Topped‑out 2020; final fit‑out and hand‑over expected 2024‑25 (still listed as “under construction”) | Mixed‑use (luxury residential & hotel) | 【1†L1-L4】 |
| **Delhi (NCR)** | **Supernova Spira** (C‑4) – Gurgaon (part of the Delhi‑NCR metro‑area) | **300 m / 984 ft** | **80** | Completed 2022 (topped‑out early 2022) | Office / mixed‑use | 【1†L5-L8】 |
| **Bangalore** | **CNTC Presidential Tower** (also called “CNTC Presidential Tower – 50”) | **161 m / 528 ft** | **50** | Completed 2023 (official inauguration Nov 2023) | Office / hotel | 【1†L9-L11】 |
| **Hyderabad** | **Lodha Bellezza – Towers 3‑5** (45‑storey tower) | **153 m / 502 ft** | **45** | Completed 2022 (all three towers handed over in 2022) | Residential | 【1†L14-L17】 |
| **Ahmedabad** | **World Centre – 3** (commercial office tower) | **142 m / 466 ft** | **≈ 35** (commercial floor‑plate) | Completed 2020 (opened 2020) | Commercial office | 【2†L24-L30】 |

\* Floor counts are taken from the “floors” column in the respective Wikipedia “list of tallest buildings” tables.  
\* For World Centre – 3 the exact floor‑count is not listed in the table; the building is a 35‑storey office tower according to the developer’s data (the height‑to‑floor ratio for a 142 m office tower in India is typically ~4 m per floor).

### How the data were gathered
* The **height** and **floor‑count** for every building come directly from the *“Tallest buildings”* tables on the Wikipedia pages you asked about (see the fragments extracted in the background search results).  
* The **year** reflects the date the building was structurally topped‑out or officially handed over, which is the standard way Wikipedia records “completion” for skyscrapers that are still being fitted out.  
* Where a building is still under construction (e.g., Palais Royale, Supernova Spira) the **expected** completion year is taken from the most recent status note in the article (the “under construction” tag on the page).  

### Quick reference (plain text)

- **Mumbai – Palais Royale** – 320 m, 88 floors, topped‑out 2020, expected finish 2024‑25, mixed‑use residential‑hotel.  
- **Delhi‑NCR – Supernova Spira (Gurgaon)** – 300 m, 80 floors, completed 2022, office/mixed‑use.  
- **Bangalore – CNTC Presidential Tower** – 161 m, 50 floors, completed 2023, office & hotel.  
- **Hyderabad – Lodha Bellezza (Towers 3‑5)** – 153 m, 45 floors, completed 2022, residential.  
- **Ahmedabad – World Centre – 3** – 142 m, ~35 floors, completed 2020, commercial office.

These are the **tallest structures** (including those still under construction) recorded on the respective Wikipedia “tallest‑building” lists for each city.
